details.description: Fireworks AI documents fireworks-asr-large, branded 'Streaming ASR v1,' as its default model for real-time speech transcription over WebSockets, and recommends it for production use where cost efficiency matters. A March 2026 capture of its model page lists it as 'Ready' for both serverless and on-demand (dedicated-GPU) use, though the page does not publish a parameter count, context length, or accuracy figures for it. As of this research date, the dedicated model page for fireworks-asr-large no longer resolves on fireworks.ai (it returns HTTP 404), so its current public status could not be confirmed on a live page.
advantages: Fireworks describes it as 'production-proven and cost-efficient' for real-time streaming transcription, positioning it as the default choice among its streaming ASR models.
Supports both serverless (pay-per-use) and on-demand dedicated-GPU deployment, per its archived Fireworks model page.
disadvantages: Fireworks' model page did not publish a parameter count, context length, or accuracy/WER figures for this model.

The dedicated fireworks.ai model page for this model returns HTTP 404 as of the research date, and Fireworks' current documentation index has no dedicated audio-transcription API page, so current availability and status could not be confirmed on a live source.
use_cases: Real-time transcription of live audio over a WebSocket connection.

sources.title: Streaming ASR v1 (fireworks-asr-large) | Fireworks AI Model Library -- Wayback Machine capture, 2026-03-14
Real-Time Speech Recognition for Enterprise Voice AI | Fireworks

notes: The live fireworks.ai/models/fireworks/fireworks-asr-large page returns HTTP 404 as of 2026-09-24 (verified directly with repeated requests), so a Wayback Machine capture of the page from 2026-03-14 -- the most recent one available -- was used as the primary source instead. The model may have been renamed, folded into an enterprise-only offering, or removed from the public self-serve library; current status could not be confirmed on a live maker page. Fireworks' current speech-recognition landing page (fetched live) describes generic 'streaming and pre-recorded audio SKUs' and names Whisper/Whisper Turbo, not fireworks-asr-large by name. Bud's catalog lists this model under the /v1/audio/transcriptions REST endpoint, while Fireworks documented it as a WebSocket-based streaming transcription API; I did not attempt to resolve this difference. No accuracy/WER or language-coverage figures were found for this specific model.
